results.corrected_title: Bloomberg: Nscale's flagship Norwegian data centre in Glomfjord is about six months late as the company prepares an IPO at up to $35bn
results.corrected_summary: Bloomberg reported on 15 October 2026 that Nscale's Glomfjord site in Norway, which is being built for ByteDance, is running about six months late. Only 6.4 MW of a planned 30 MW is operating. The delay follows repeated cooling leaks, a December transformer fire after which Norway's Directorate for Civil Protection (DSB) found 10 safety violations, and slow construction. The coverage also says grid capacity for a major expansion in Korgen may not arrive much before 2037. Nscale filed on 18 September to list on the NYSE under the ticker NSCL, seeking up to $3bn at a valuation of up to $35bn, more than double the $14.6bn valuation of its March round led by Aker and 8090 Industries.
key_facts: Glomfjord is about six months behind schedule, with 6.4 MW of a planned 30 MW running
DSB found 10 safety violations after a December fire; Nscale fixed them and the case was closed in September
Grid capacity for a major Korgen expansion is unlikely much before 2037
IPO filing on 18 September for the NYSE (NSCL): up to $3bn raised at a valuation of up to $35bn, versus $14.6bn in the March round
More than $103bn in contracts, about 85% of it from Microsoft and Anthropic
results.issues: I could not open the Bloomberg article itself (paywalled); the facts come from secondary write-ups of it. Penalties are disputed. Glomfjord customers were reportedly offered better terms on new contracts instead of cash penalties. The penalties worth millions owed to Microsoft relate to the Sines site in Portugal. DCD, citing a source close to the project, says no fines were imposed for Glomfjord. Do not say 'penalties' about Glomfjord without that nuance.

results.corrected_title: Goldman beats sharply and sees a big AI financing opportunity; JPMorgan misses estimates and restricts outside AI agents
results.corrected_summary: On 13 October 2026 Goldman Sachs reported Q3 net revenues of $18.68bn and diluted EPS of $17.01, well above consensus. CEO David Solomon called AI infrastructure financing a major opportunity but warned of a possible reset if data centres are overbuilt. JPMorgan's results came in below expectations: net income was $15.3bn ($5.57 per share), and revenue was $50.2bn reported or $50.9bn managed. Jamie Dimon said outside AI agents will not get unrestricted access to the bank's internal systems, and CFO Jeremy Barnum said productivity gains from AI are not yet visible in quarterly results. Morgan Stanley beat estimates on 14 October with $20.3bn in revenue.
key_facts: Goldman Q3 (13 Oct): net revenues $18.68bn, diluted EPS $17.01, net earnings $5.29bn
Solomon: 'There is going to be a lot of financing to do, and we're going to be in the middle of that', while warning of a possible AI-infrastructure reset
JPMorgan Q3: net income $15.3bn, EPS $5.57 (vs about $5.90 expected), managed revenue $50.9bn vs about $51.2bn expected
Dimon: outside AI agents will not get unrestricted access to JPMorgan's internal systems
Barnum: AI productivity gains are not yet visible in quarterly results
Morgan Stanley Q3 (14 Oct): net revenues $20.3bn, EPS $3.03 vs $2.83 consensus
results.issues: The candidate mixes JPMorgan figures. $50.17bn is reported revenue, but the roughly $51.2bn consensus applies to managed revenue ($50.9bn); Zacks cites a different consensus ($52.21bn). The '~30% above estimate' for Goldman is unclear because sources give different consensus figures, so leave it out. Morgan Stanley reported on 14 October, not 13 October. The Dimon and Barnum remarks are paraphrased in secondary sources, not direct quotes, and Barnum said 'AI', not specifically 'genAI'. CNBC returned 403, so I could not open it.

results.corrected_title: WSJ: Amazon in talks to buy Israeli AI startup Decart for about $7bn
results.corrected_summary: The Wall Street Journal reported on 12 October 2026 that Amazon is in talks to acquire Decart, an Israeli AI startup, in a deal worth about $7bn that could close soon if talks do not collapse. Decart makes world models (Lucy, Oasis) and software that lets developers move AI workloads between different chips. It was valued at nearly $4bn in a $300m round in May 2026 led by Radical Ventures, with Nvidia among the participants. Anthropic earlier discussed buying it for about $6bn but reportedly walked away after due diligence.
key_facts: WSJ report on 12 Oct 2026: Amazon in talks to buy Decart for about $7bn; no deal confirmed
Decart was founded in 2023 by Dean and Orian Leitersdorf and Moshe Shalev
May 2026: $300m round led by Radical Ventures, with Nvidia participating, at a valuation of nearly $4bn
Anthropic earlier held talks at about $6bn and reportedly abandoned them after due diligence
AWS gave Decart early access to its Trainium3 chip in 2025
results.issues: I did not open the WSJ original; the claims rest on two secondary reports of it. Ynetnews says both Nvidia and Anthropic were interested in buying Decart and that those talks collapsed, while American Bazaar names only Anthropic as a would-be buyer and Nvidia as an investor. This is a report of talks only, not a completed deal.
